prompt:
Review these user stories and provide UX/UI advice:
- DASH-01: As a cluster operator, I want a Kanban-style layout with drag-and-drop cards so that I can visually organize and prioritize Kubernetes workloads by status
  Given the Rufkis dashboard is loaded
 And the Kanban board displays columns: "Pending", "Running", "Failed", "Unknown"
When I drag a card from "Pending" to "Running"
Then the card snaps into the "Running" column
 And the underlying resource status changes to Running
 And a success toast appears

Given the user has dragged a card
When the backend update fails
Then the card returns to its original column
 And an error toast appears
- DASH-02: As a cluster operator, I want live status indicators per Kubernetes cluster node so that I can instantly detect node-level anomalies without refreshing
  Given the Rufkis dashboard is rendering cluster nodes
When a node's Ready condition transitions from True to False
Then the card's status indicator changes from green to red within 5 seconds
 And a tooltip displays: "Node lost heartbeat at <timestamp>"

Given a node has not reported for 60 seconds
When the node transitions to Unknown
Then the indicator changes to amber
 And a tooltip: "Node has not reported since <timestamp>"
- DASH-03: As a cluster operator, I want an embedded terminal panel with direct kubectl access so that I can execute ad-hoc commands without switching context
  Given I am on the Rufkis dashboard
When I click the terminal icon or press Ctrl+`
Then an embedded terminal panel opens at the bottom
 And the active cluster context is in the prompt

Given the terminal panel is open
When I type "kubectl get pods" and press Enter
Then output streams in real time
 And the command is audited

Given the terminal is idle for 15 minutes
When timeout elapses
Then the session auto-terminates
 And the panel collapses
- DASH-04: As a cluster operator, I want to filter the Kanban board by namespace so that I can focus on workloads in a specific scope
  Given the Rufkis dashboard shows all namespaces
When I select "production" from the filter dropdown
Then only cards with namespace="production" are visible
 And the health summary recalculates for that scope

Given the filter is set to "production"
When I clear the filter
Then all namespace cards are shown
 And the health summary returns to cluster scope
- DASH-05: As a cluster operator, I want a cluster health summary bar at the top so that I can assess overall cluster status at a glance
  Given the Rufkis dashboard is loaded
Then a health summary bar displays:
 | Total Nodes | Ready X / NotReady Y / Unknown Z |
 | Total Pods  | Running A / Pending B / Failed C |
 | Cluster Version | v1.28.x |
 | Uptime | Xd Yh Zm |

When a node transitions from Ready to NotReady
Then the summary updates within 5 seconds
 And Ready -1, NotReady +1

When the namespace filter is active
Then the summary reflects only that namespace's resources
- DASH-06: As a cluster operator, I want a dark/light theme toggle so that I can reduce eye strain during extended monitoring sessions
  Given the Rufkis dashboard is open in light mode
When I click the moon icon in the header
Then the UI switches to dark mode instantly
 And the icon changes to a sun icon
 And the preference is persisted in localStorage

Given dark mode was selected
When I reload the page
Then the page loads in dark mode
 And no flash of incorrect theme occurs
